jobs.description:
The Director, Performance Management & Capabilities Building is a strategic leader responsible for defining and executing Sonova’s global learning, performance management, and talent development strategies. This role oversees the design and implementation of the Academies framework, coaching and mentoring programmes—including AI-enabled approaches—graduate development, and scalable learning offerings that build organisational capability at all levels.

Accountable for shaping and embedding a robust performance management framework, this role partners closely with senior leaders to drive goal setting and talent development for Sonova’s Top 200+ leaders, ensuring alignment with business priorities and leadership standards. The Director leads flagship talent development programmes, individual career journey design, and the talent review process, fostering a culture of continuous growth and high performance.

This role ensures integration and alignment of learning and performance initiatives with broader talent functions such as talent acquisition, culture transformation, and Org E&E. The Director also collaborates with HR Strategy to develop and maintain a comprehensive skills architecture and taxonomy that supports Sonova’s evolving capability needs.

In this role, you will:

Lead Learning and Academies

• Define, develop, and oversee the global Academies framework and its implementation to build critical capabilities across Sonova.

• Design and deliver coaching and mentoring programmes, incorporating AI-enabled tools and approaches to enhance learning effectiveness.

• Manage graduate programmes and scalable learning offerings to support talent development at all organisational levels.

Drive Performance Management Framework

• Own and continuously evolve Sonova’s performance management framework, ensuring alignment with organisational goals and leadership expectations.

• Lead goal-setting processes for the Top 200 leaders, fostering accountability and clear performance expectations.

• Partner with HR and business leaders to embed performance management practices that drive high performance and development.

Talent Development and Career Journey Design

• Lead the design and execution of individual career journeys for Sonova’s Top 200 talent, supporting personalised growth and succession planning.

• Oversee flagship talent development programmes, including approach design, assessment methodologies, and delivery.

• Develop and implement people leadership standards and related development programmes to strengthen leadership capabilities across the organisation.

Talent Review and Succession Processes

• Manage the talent review approach and processes, ensuring robust assessment and calibration of talent across business units.

• Collaborate with HR Strategy and Org E&E team to align talent development efforts with organisational capability needs and succession plans.

Skills Architecture and Taxonomy

• Partner with HR Strategy to develop, maintain, and evolve a comprehensive skills architecture and taxonomy that supports workforce planning and capability building.

• Ensure skills frameworks are integrated into learning, performance management, and talent development initiatives.

Stakeholder Engagement and Collaboration

• Work closely with business leaders, HR Business Partners, and the Talent Centre of Excellence to ensure learning and performance strategies are aligned with business priorities.

• Collaborate with external partners, including business schools and learning providers, to enhance programme quality and innovation.

• Manage vendor relationships and oversee quality management systems for external learning and assessment providers.

Innovation and Continuous Improvement

• Champion a culture of continuous learning and development, leveraging digital and multimedia solutions to maximise reach and impact.

• Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness, adoption, and compliance of learning and performance programmes, using data to drive improvements.

• Stay abreast of industry trends and best practices to ensure Sonova remains a leader in leadership development and talent management.

Your Profile:

• 12+ years of progressive leadership experience in global learning, leadership development, and performance management, with a proven track record of designing and scaling high-impact talent development programmes in complex, matrixed organisations.

• Master’s degree in Psychology, Human Resources, Business, or a related field; formal training or qualification in talent development or coaching is highly desirable.

• Ability to develop and execute integrated learning and performance strategies that align with business objectives, drive organisational transformation, and foster a culture of continuous development and high performance.

• Deep knowledge of leadership models, coaching methodologies (including AI-enabled coaching), and talent development frameworks, with experience leading flagship programmes for senior and emerging leaders.

• Strong analytical skills with expertise in leveraging learning analytics, programme evaluation, and performance data to inform strategy, optimise learning experiences, and demonstrate measurable business impact.

• Exceptional stakeholder management and internal consulting skills, with a proven ability to influence senior executives and cross-functional leaders, champion change initiatives, and navigate organisational complexity with agility and resilience.

• Skilled in designing blended learning solutions that incorporate digital, experiential, and social learning modalities at scale, utilising cutting-edge technologies and platforms to enhance engagement and accessibility.

• Experience leading diverse, geographically dispersed teams and programmes across multiple regions (EMEA, Americas, APAC), with sensitivity to cultural nuances and local market dynamics.

• Proven capability in managing budgets, vendor relationships, and quality assurance processes to deliver cost-effective, scalable, and compliant learning and performance management solutions.

• Expertise in learning management systems (e.g., SuccessFactors) and other digital tools that support learning analytics and talent development

• Outstanding communication, presentation, and facilitation skills, capable of engaging and inspiring audiences at all organisational levels, from store sales employees to C-suite executives

• Proven experience designing and implementing diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives within learning and talent development strategies to build inclusive leadership capabilities.

• Experience working within a corporate headquarters environment, collaborating closely with HR Centres of Excellence, business leaders, and external partners such as business schools and learning providers

• English is a must; proficiency in multiple languages is an asset.

More about what we offer

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both your professional and personal development, and there are exceptional growth opportunities with individual development plans.

For this vacancy, only direct applications will be considered.

jobs.title: Hardware Verification Specialist
jobs.description:
At Sonova, we create innovative hearing care solutions that improve the quality of life for millions of people worldwide. As a Hardware Verification Specialist, you will help ensure the quality, reliability, and performance of our hearing aids and accessories before they reach customers.

Working in a collaborative R&D environment, you will combine hands-on technical work with problem-solving and testing, contributing directly to products that make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

More about the role

In this role, you will:

• Execute hardware verification tests on hearing aids, accessories, and assemblies

• Perform acoustic, electronic, mechanical, and chemical measurements using specialized laboratory equipment

• Analyze test results and document findings in technical reports

• Support the development and improvement of test methods, verification processes, and laboratory structures

• Investigate unusual test behaviors and collaborate with engineers to identify root causes

• Maintain laboratory equipment and support day-to-day lab operations

• Contribute to R&D activities, team collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement initiatives

More about you

You are a hands-on and detail-oriented professional who enjoys understanding how electronic products work and finding reliable ways to verify their performance. You combine technical curiosity with a structured and quality-focused approach to your work.

Must-Have

• Technical education in Electronics, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

• Hands-on experience with manufacturing, repair, servicing, or troubleshooting electronic devices

• Practical experience with soldering and working with small electronic or electromechanical components

• Strong knowledge of electronics and measurement technologies

• Good English and German communication skills (written and spoken)

• Proactive, quality-focused, and eager to learn

Nice to have

• Experience in hardware verification, testing, or validation

• Experience in medical devices or other regulated industries

• Knowledge of acoustic measurements

• Experience in results documentation

• Familiarity with Confluence and MS Teams

More about what we offer

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both your professional and personal development, and there are exceptional growth opportunities with individual development plans.

Magdalena Suszek, Talent Acquisition Partner, is looking forward to receiving your application (cover letter, CV, references and certificates) via our online job application platform.

For this vacancy only direct applications will be considered.

A Sonova, creiamo soluzioni innovative per la cura dell'udito che migliorano la qualità della vita per milioni di persone in tutto il mondo. In qualità di Specialista di verifica hardware, vi aiuterà a garantire la qualità, l'affidabilità e le prestazioni dei nostri apparecchi acustici e accessori prima che raggiungano i clienti. Lavorando in un ambiente R&D collaborativo, si unirà al lavoro tecnico pratico con problem solving e test, contribuendo direttamente a prodotti che fanno una differenza significativa nella vita delle persone. Ulteriori informazioni sul ruolo In questo ruolo, voi:
• Eseguire test di verifica hardware sugli apparecchi acustici, sugli accessori e sugli assemblaggi
• Eseguire misurazioni acustiche, elettroniche, meccaniche e chimiche utilizzando attrezzature di laboratorio specializzate
• Analizzare i risultati dei test e i risultati dei documenti nelle relazioni tecniche
• Sostenere lo sviluppo e il miglioramento dei metodi di prova, dei processi di verifica e delle strutture di laboratorio
• Indagare comportamenti di test insoliti e collaborare con gli ingegneri per identificare le cause della radice
• Mantenere le attrezzature di laboratorio e sostenere le operazioni di laboratorio quotidiane
• Contribuire a attività R&D, collaborazione di team, condivisione di conoscenze e iniziative di miglioramento continuo Più di te Sei un professionista pratico e orientato al dettaglio che gode di capire come i prodotti elettronici funzionano e trovare modi affidabili per verificare le loro prestazioni. Unisci la curiosità tecnica con un approccio strutturato e orientato alla qualità al tuo lavoro. Devo...
• Istruzione tecnica in Elettronica, Meccatronica, Ingegneria Elettrica, o un campo correlato
• Esperienza pratica con la produzione, la riparazione, la manutenzione o la risoluzione dei problemi di dispositivi elettronici

More about the role

In this role, you will:

• Execute hardware verification tests on hearing aids, accessories, and assemblies

• Perform acoustic, electronic, mechanical, and chemical measurements using specialized laboratory equipment

• Analyze test results and document findings in technical reports

• Support the development and improvement of test methods, verification processes, and laboratory structures

Dabei treibst du kontinuierliche Verbesserungen im Bereich Maintenance voran und entwickelst deine Fachkenntnisse (z. B. im TPS) stetig weiter.

Als technische Schnittstelle zwischen Produktion, Engineering und Entwicklung unterstützt du die Fachbereiche, berätst bei technischen Fragestellungen und wirkst an der Optimierung unserer Anlagen mit.

• Sicherstellung der Anlagenverfügbarkeit durch vorbeugende Wartung von Anlagen, Betriebs- und Prüfmitteln

• Analyse und Behebung von Störungen in der Produktion inklusive Ursachenanalyse

• Kontinuierliche Verbesserung (Continuous Improvement) im Bereich Maintenance

• Technische Schnittstelle zwischen Produktion, Engineering, Entwicklung sowie weiteren Fachbereichen (R&D, NPI, B&I)

• Technische Beratung und Unterstützung der Produktionsabteilungen sowie Mitwirkung bei der Optimierung von Anlagen

• Koordination, Dokumentation und Überwachung von Instandhaltungsmaßnahmen (inkl. LEXA) sowie Einhaltung von Qualitäts- und Sicherheitsvorschriften

• Verwaltung und Beschaffung von Ersatzteilen sowie Unterstützung bei der Weiterentwicklung automatisierter Anlagen und Pikettdienst bei Bedarf

Mehr über dich

• Abgeschlossene technische Berufsbildung (EFZ) im elektronischen Bereich (z. B. Automatiker, Polymechaniker, Elektroniker)

• Erfahrung in der Elektronikproduktion, idealerweise mit Kenntnissen in Lean Management, Supply Chain und SMD/Flip-Chip-Bestückung

• Gute Übersicht über die gesamte Produktionskette sowie idealerweise Erfahrung in der Automatisierung oder Halbleiterfertigung

Als eines der weltweit führenden Unternehmen im Bereich Hörlösungen mit Hauptsitz in der Schweiz legen wir großen Wert auf eine inklusive und wertschätzende Unternehmenskultur.

jobs.description:
At Sonova, we create innovative hearing solutions that improve the lives of millions of people worldwide. To strengthen our commitment to delivering exceptional product quality and customer experience, we are looking for a Director Reliability Engineering to lead our reliability strategy, build organizational capability, and drive reliability excellence across the full product lifecycle.

In this highly visible leadership role, you will combine people leadership, technical problem-solving, and strategic product reliability planning. You will lead a team of reliability engineers, partner with stakeholders across R&D, Quality, Operations and Product Management, and ensure reliability is embedded into both current products and future innovations.

More about the role

• Lead, develop, and structure a high-performing Reliability Engineering team, establishing effective operating models, governance, and best practices.

• Drive complex product reliability investigations, root cause analyses, and failure assessments of field returns and customer complaints, translating findings into actionable improvement plans.

• Partner with key customers and internal stakeholders to communicate technical findings, present recommendations, and feed reliability learnings back into product development.

• Define and execute Sonova’s reliability engineering strategy, ensuring Design for Reliability principles, methods, and decision-making are embedded from concept through design, verification, industrialization, and lifecycle management.

• Establish and continuously improve reliability methodologies, including D-FMEA, Critical-to-Quality frameworks, reliability planning & accelerated life testing, and data-driven failure analysis.

• Identify reliability risks and opportunities within the innovation pipeline, proactively assessing future products and technologies before market launch.

• Lead cross-functional improvement initiatives that enhance product robustness, customer satisfaction, and long-term business performance.

• Foster a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and reliability excellence across the organization.

More about you

• Degree in Engineering, Physics, Electronics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 5+ years of leadership experience in Product Reliability Engineering, Reliability Testing, Quality Engineering, or a closely related field.

• Proven track record of leading and developing engineering teams, establishing structures, processes, and ways of working that enable scalability and performance.

• Strong expertise in root cause analysis, design for reliability, failure investigation, and product improvement methodologies.

• Experience working in highly regulated and quality-driven industries such as medical devices, automotive, aerospace, industrial electronics, or similar.

• Ability to influence senior stakeholders and communicate complex technical topics to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Strategic mindset with the ability to balance operational execution, customer-facing activities, and long-term product reliability planning.

• Fluent English communication skills.

• Knowledge of medical device regulations is advantageous.

More about what we offer:

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both your professional and personal development, and there are exceptional growth opportunities with individual development plans.

Application process

Magdalena Suszek, Talent Acquisition Partner, is looking forward to receiving your application via our online job application platform, including your CV and cover letter. For this vacancy, only direct applications will be considered

• Établir et améliorer continuellement les méthodes de fiabilité, y compris le D-FMEA, les cadres critiques à la qualité, la planification de la fiabilité et les essais accélérés de la vie, et l'analyse de défaillance fondée sur les données.

• Diplôme en génie, physique, électronique, génie mécanique ou un domaine technique connexe.
• 5+ ans d'expérience de leadership en Ingénierie de Fiabilité des Produits, Tests de Fiabilité, Ingénierie de Qualité, ou un domaine étroitement lié.
• Expérience éprouvée d'équipes de direction et de développement d'ingénierie, en établissant des structures, des processus et des méthodes de travail qui permettent l'évolutivité et la performance.
• Une solide expertise dans l'analyse des causes profondes, la conception de la fiabilité, les enquêtes sur les défaillances et les méthodes d'amélioration des produits.
• Expérience de travail dans des industries hautement réglementées et axées sur la qualité telles que les appareils médicaux, l'automobile, l'aérospatiale, l'électronique industrielle, ou similaire.
• Capacité d'influencer les principaux intervenants et de communiquer des sujets techniques complexes à des auditoires techniques et non techniques.
• Un état d'esprit stratégique avec la capacité d'équilibrer l'exécution opérationnelle, les activités orientées vers le client et la planification à long terme de la fiabilité des produits.
• Compétences de communication en anglais.

Deine Rolle bei uns

In dieser Funktion bist du die fachliche Führung im Support-Team der Elektronikproduktion (m/w/d) und die personelle Führung als Stellvertreter in der Abwesenheit des Teamleiters. Dein Arbeitsalltag bewegt sich direkt an unseren Surface Mount Technology (SMT)-Linien und im Umfeld der Automated Optical Inspection (AOI).

Du unterstützt den stabilen Produktionsbetrieb, bist eine wichtige Ansprechperson auf dem Shopfloor und bringst dein technisches Verständnis sowie deine Erfahrung aktiv in die Weiterentwicklung unserer Prozesse ein.

More about the role

• Fachliche Unterstützung und Koordination der Mitarbeitenden (m/w/d) im Produktionsalltag sowie Stellvertretung des Teamleiters bei Abwesenheit

• Aktive Mitarbeit im laufenden Betrieb der Surface Mount Technology (SMT)

• Unterstützung, Bedienung und Absicherung der Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) inklusive Pausenablösungen und Springerfunktion

• Analyse von Störungen und erste Maßnahmen zur Behebung in enger Zusammenarbeit mit technischen Schnittstellen

• Organisation von Schichtübergaben sowie Mitarbeit im Daily Management (Tier Meeting)

• Aktive Beteiligung an Continuous-Improvement-, 5S- und Kaizen-Aktivitäten

• Sicherstellung eines klaren Informationsflusses und Durchführung von Gemba-Rundgängen

More about you

• Abgeschlossene anerkannte Berufsausbildung im technischen oder industriellen Umfeld

• Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung in der Elektronikproduktion, idealerweise im Umfeld der Surface Mount Technology (SMT)

• Vertraut im Umgang mit Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) und den zugehörigen Produktionsprozessen

• Ausgeprägtes Qualitätsbewusstsein und strukturierte Arbeitsweise

• Teamorientierte Persönlichkeit (m/w/d) mit Freude an fachlicher Verantwortung

• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift, Englischkenntnisse von Vorteil

• Programmierung Kenntnisse und IPC Zertifikat von Vorteil

More about what we offer

Als eines der weltweit führenden Unternehmen im Bereich Hörlösungen mit Hauptsitz in der Schweiz legen wir großen Wert auf eine inklusive und wertschätzende Unternehmenskultur.

• Flexible Anstellungsmöglichkeiten (80–100 %)

• Strukturierte Einarbeitung sowie gezielte interne und externe Weiterbildungen

jobs.description:
Sonova is seeking a Senior Manager, RIC and BTE Solutions to lead the development and delivery of signal processing solutions across RIC and BTE hearing products. This role provides technical, functional, and people leadership to ensure scalable, high-quality, and product-ready software solutions that support Sonova’s global hearing system platforms.

More about the role

• Lead and own the development, design and integration of signal processing features for Sonova hearing systems

• Provide technical leadership and decision-making authority for signal processing realization

• Drive reuse, scalability, and product readiness across platforms, products, and Sonova brands

• Establish clear cross domain alignment and decision making across departments and areas

• Collaborate closely with Product Management and Project Leaders to ensure customer focus and success in the market

• Lead, develop, and manage a team of software professionals while supporting talent development and succession planning

More about you

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Software Engineering, Systems Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline

• Proven leadership experience in software development and in people leadership within complex R&D environments

• Extensive experience shaping and delivering software features across multiple platforms, product generations, and releases

• Strong understanding of Digital Signal Processing (DSP), system integration, fitting software systems, and regulated product development

• Ability to lead through ambiguity while balancing innovation, scalability, quality, and long-term platform value

• Strong, confident communicator with demonstrated soft skills applied to leadership and collaboration across technical, audiological, and business stakeholders

• Experience working in international, multi-site, and cross-functional environments

• Curious about emerging technologies, particularly AI, with a forward-looking mindset and passion for innovation

• Fluent in English; German is a plus

More about what we offer:

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both your professional and personal development, and there are exceptional growth opportunities with individual development plans.

At Sonova, you'll join a global team of innovators dedicated to transforming lives through cutting-edge hearing technology. You'll have the opportunity to:

• Shape the future of signal processing across multiple global hearing instrument brands.

• Lead talented international engineering teams working on technologies that improve the lives of millions of people worldwide.

• Influence long-term platform strategy and drive innovation in a collaborative, global R&D environment.

• Work with passionate experts in software engineering, signal processing, audiology, and product development.

• Grow your career while making a meaningful impact on the future of hearing healthcare.

Application process

Magdalena Suszek, Talent Acquisition Partner, is looking forward to receiving your application via our online job application platform, including your CV and cover letter. For this vacancy, only direct applications will be considered

Help shape how quality is engineered into products used by millions of people worldwide.

At Sonova, we're looking for an experienced quality leader to own and evolve our global Critical-to-Quality (CtQ) framework, ensuring the product characteristics most critical to customer satisfaction, reliability, safety and regulatory compliance are embedded throughout the entire product lifecycle.

Working across R&D, Manufacturing, Operations, Supplier Quality and Service, you will establish global quality governance, drive end-to-end traceability and help shape how innovative hearing solutions are developed over the full product lifecycle.

If you enjoy building frameworks, train people, working together with other stakeholders and driving continuous improvement in a highly regulated environment, we would love to hear from you.

More about the role

• Own and continuously evolve Sonova's global Critical-to-Quality (CtQ) framework, ensuring its implementation and effectiveness across the entire product lifecycle.

• Establish and drive global CtQ governance, standards and best practices across product development, manufacturing and service.

• Lead cross-functional CtQ reviews, aligning R&D, Manufacturing, Supplier Quality and Service around critical quality goals.

• Ensure end-to-end traceability of Critical-to-Quality attributes from design to manufacturing and service.

• Integrate CtQ into key quality processes, including Design-, Process-, Service FMEA and Safety Risk Management.

• Ensure field performance, reliability and customer insights will feed back to CtQs to continuously improve product quality and future product generations.

• Drive continuous improvement of CtQ methodologies, tools and KPIs.

• Train stakeholders on how to apply CtQ principles.

More about you

• A degree in Engineering, Quality, Science or another technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

• Extensive experience in Quality, Product Development, Manufacturing or Operational Excellence within a highly regulated industry, ideally Medical Devices, Aerospace or Automotive.

• Hands-on experience leading the practical application of APQP, PPAP, FMEA and lean initiatives to improve overall product quality.

• Strong knowledge of Quality Management System setup g. ISO 9001; experience with ISO 13485, ISO 14971 and IEC 62304 is an advantage.

• A track record of leading cross-functional quality or continuous improvement initiatives and influencing stakeholders in complex, global organizations.

• A curious, pragmatic and entrepreneurial mindset, combined with excellent stakeholder management, communication and presentation skills.

• Fluent English; German is a plus.

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we are committed to building an inclusive culture where you can balance a successful career with your life outside of work through our flexible hybrid working model. jobs.description:
Shape the future of how millions of people experience hearing

At Sonova, we believe exceptional hearing solutions are about much more than outstanding technology—they're about creating products people trust, enjoy wearing and rely on every day.

As Director Anatomic and Acoustic Design RIC-BTE, you'll lead the development of Fit-and-Go sound delivery systems across Sonova's hearing instrument portfolio, shaping solutions that combine excellent hearing performance with wearing comfort, discretion and ease of everyday use. By translating customer needs, anatomical diversity and product intent into scalable, reliable and manufacturable solutions, you'll play a key role in strengthening customer satisfaction, product differentiation and Sonova's competitive advantage.

Leading a team of highly skilled experts, you'll work at the intersection of engineering, acoustics, anatomy and user-centred design, collaborating across global R&D to define the next generation of sound delivery systems for multiple brands, products and technology platforms.

More about the role

• Lead the development of Fit-and-Go sound delivery systems and acoustic coupling solutions across Sonova's hearing instrument portfolio, from concept through product release.

• Shape customer-centric solutions that balance hearing performance, wearing comfort, discretion, durability and everyday usability while addressing the diversity of ear anatomy and real-world customer needs.

• Define scalable, platform-oriented concepts that enable reuse across products, brands and future technology generations.

• Partner closely with Mechanical Design, Hardware Integration, Hearing Performance, Materials & Biological Safety, Industrial Design and other cross-functional teams to ensure successful product development and industrialization.

• Drive innovation by translating customer insights, clinical learnings and emerging technologies into differentiated product solutions that deliver lasting customer value.

• Build, coach and develop a high-performing global team, fostering technical excellence, collaboration and long-term capability development.

• Lead cross-functional decision-making, balancing customer value, technical feasibility, manufacturability and business priorities to successfully bring innovative solutions to market.

• Champion a collaborative culture that strengthens platform ownership, knowledge sharing and innovation across Sonova's global R&D organization.

More about you

Must have

• Engineering background with proven experience leading product development within a complex, multidisciplinary R&D environment.

• Demonstrated leadership experience building, coaching and developing high-performing technical teams in an international, multi-site organization.

• Strong experience developing innovative products from concept through industrialization and manufacturing.

• Proven ability to translate customer needs into differentiated technical solutions while balancing performance, manufacturability, scalability and business objectives.

• Strong systems thinking, strategic mindset and the ability to navigate complex technical and organizational challenges.

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence across engineering, product, clinical and business functions.

• Passion for innovation, customer-centric product development and collaborative leadership.

• Fluent English language skills.

Nice to have

• Knowledge of acoustics, ear anatomy, user-centred design and/or medical device development.

• Leadership, organizational development or transformation training.

• Knowledge of medical device regulations and validation frameworks.

• Experience with Jira, Confluence, portfolio management tools and data-driven product development environments.

• German language skills.

More about what we offer

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we are committed to building an inclusive culture where you can balance a successful career with your life outside of work through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both professional and personal development, with strong growth opportunities supported by individual development plans.

Application process

Magdalena Suszek, Talent Acquisition Partner, is looking forward to receiving your application via our online job application platform, including your CV and cover letter. For this vacancy, only direct applications will be considered.

jobs.title: Global Head of Intellectual Property
jobs.description:
Sonova is a global leader in innovative hearing care solutions, dedicated to improving lives through technology. Intellectual Property is a critical strategic asset that underpins our innovation leadership, competitive differentiation, and long-term business success.

We are seeking a Global Head of Intellectual Property to lead Sonova's global intellectual property strategy and governance framework. This is a highly visible enterprise leadership role operating at the intersection of Legal, R&D, innovation, and business strategy.

The execuitve will serve as the enterprise owner of IP strategy, risk management, enforcement, licensing strategy, and governance across both hard and soft IP. Working in close partnership with R&D leadership, the leader will ensure that intellectual property is fully integrated into technology planning, innovation pipelines, product roadmaps, and business decision-making.

The successful candidate will lead a global IP organization through experienced team leaders and external partners while serving as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on matters that impact innovation, competitive positioning, and enterprise value creation.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise IP Strategy & Leadership

• Define, develop, and continuously evolve Sonova's global intellectual property strategy, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives, innovation priorities, and market positioning.

• Serve as the principal advisor to the General Counsel, Executive Committee members, R&D leadership, and senior business leaders on intellectual property matters.

• Own enterprise-wide IP governance, risk management, and strategic decision-making across patents, trade secrets, trademarks, copyrights, and related intellectual property assets.

• Lead and develop senior IP professionals while fostering a business-oriented and strategically focused IP culture.

• Shape the future evolution of Sonova's IP function, capabilities, operating model, and external partnerships.

Strategic Partnership with R&D

• Serve as the primary strategic interface between the Legal and R&D organizations on all intellectual property matters.

• Ensure IP strategy is embedded throughout innovation processes, technology planning, product development, and long-term technology roadmaps.

• Maintain a permanent strategic presence within innovation planning and technology governance forums to identify and protect key innovations at the earliest stages of development.

• Guide strategic decisions concerning patents, trade secrets, design rights, publication strategies, open innovation initiatives, and alternative protection mechanisms.

• Partner closely with R&D leadership to ensure effective operation of invention harvesting processes, IP stage-gates, freedom-to-operate reviews, and technical risk assessments.

Portfolio Strategy & Investment Governance

• Establish the strategic direction for Sonova's global patent and design portfolio.

• Ensure portfolio investments are aligned with business priorities, technology trends, and competitive differentiation objectives.

• Oversee portfolio development, prosecution strategy, maintenance decisions, and lifecycle management through experienced internal teams and external counsel.

• Regularly assess portfolio strength, geographic coverage, white-space opportunities, competitive positioning, and emerging risks.

• Drive a disciplined approach to maximizing portfolio value and return on investment.

Competitive Intelligence & Strategic Risk Assessment

• Direct Sonova's IP-based competitive intelligence strategy, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities and technology objectives.

• Oversee strategic freedom-to-operate, clearance, and risk management frameworks across the organization.

• Translate complex competitive IP landscapes into actionable strategic recommendations for executive leadership.

• Monitor significant industry, regulatory, technological, and competitive developments impacting Sonova's innovation strategy.

• Identify opportunities for portfolio strengthening, strategic acquisitions, partnerships, licensing opportunities, and risk mitigation.

Licensing, Partnerships & Value Creation

• Lead the company's strategy for licensing, cross-licensing, technology partnerships, and other IP-based value creation initiatives.

• Support strategic commercial negotiations where intellectual property is a key business asset.

• Provide strategic IP leadership in M&A transactions, partnerships, collaborations, and technology investments.

• Evaluate opportunities to leverage Sonova's intellectual property portfolio as a competitive and commercial advantage.

Disputes, Enforcement & Litigation Strategy

• Define and direct Sonova's global strategy for IP enforcement, defense, and dispute resolution.

• Oversee significant patent, trademark, copyright, advertising, and technology-related disputes worldwide.

• Manage external counsel and expert advisors supporting contentious IP matters.

• Advise executive leadership on risk exposure, litigation strategy, settlement considerations, and business impacts.

• Ensure alignment between litigation strategy, portfolio development, and broader business objectives.

Soft IP Governance & Brand Protection

• Oversee enterprise management of trademarks, copyrights, brand protection, marketing claims, and related intellectual property matters.

• Ensure effective collaboration between Legal, Marketing, and Commercial functions to protect and enhance Sonova's brand assets.

• Establish frameworks that enable early review, clearance, and protection of brand and product naming initiatives.

• Support the development and protection of valuable intangible assets across the business.

Governance & Enterprise Risk Management

• Establish and maintain robust IP governance frameworks, policies, processes, and decision-making standards.

• Chair or actively participate in cross-functional governance forums responsible for intellectual property strategy, prioritization, and resource alignment.

• Ensure consistent and proactive management of IP-related risks across jurisdictions and business functions.

• Promote enterprise-wide awareness of intellectual property as a strategic business asset.

• Ensure effective utilization of external counsel, service providers, and supporting resources.

More about you:

• Advanced degree (JD, PhD, LLM, MSc Engineering, or equivalent) in a legal, scientific, engineering, or technical discipline.

• 15+ years of progressive intellectual property experience with significant exposure to patent strategy and counseling.

• Demonstrated success operating at a senior strategic level and influencing executive leadership and R&D organizations.

• Deep understanding of global patent systems and broader intellectual property frameworks.

• Experience leading IP organizations through senior professionals and external partners.

• Strong commercial orientation with the ability to balance legal, technical, business, and innovation considerations.

• Proven experience managing complex cross-functional stakeholder environments.

Preferred previous experience

• Experience within a multinational technology, healthcare, medical device, electronics, software, or innovation-driven organization.

• Significant experience in patent litigation, enforcement, oppositions, or dispute management in the US and Europe.

• Demonstrated success supporting strategic licensing, cross-licensing, technology transactions, collaborations, or M&A activities.

• Familiarity with U.S., European, and Asian intellectual property systems and regulatory environments.

• Experience partnering closely with engineering and R&D organizations in highly innovative environments.

Why Join Sonova

This is a rare opportunity to shape the intellectual property strategy of a global innovation leader operating at the intersection of healthcare and technology.

You will have direct influence on innovation strategy, technology direction, competitive positioning, and enterprise value creation while partnering closely with world-class R&D, legal, and business leaders. The role offers exceptional visibility, meaningful impact, and the opportunity to help define the future of intellectual property at Sonova.

Sonova is a global leader in innovative hearing care solutions, dedicated to improving lives through technology. Intellectual Property is a critical strategic asset that underpins our innovation leadership, competitive differentiation, and long-term business success.

We are seeking a Global Head of Intellectual Property to lead Sonova's global intellectual property strategy and governance framework. This is a highly visible enterprise leadership role operating at the intersection of Legal, R&D, innovation, and business strategy.

The execuitve will serve as the enterprise owner of IP strategy, risk management, enforcement, licensing strategy, and governance across both hard and soft IP. Working in close partnership with R&D leadership, the leader will ensure that intellectual property is fully integrated into technology planning, innovation pipelines, product roadmaps, and business decision-making.

The successful candidate will lead a global IP organization through experienced team leaders and external partners while serving as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on matters that impact innovation, competitive positioning, and enterprise value creation.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise IP Strategy & Leadership

• Define, develop, and continuously evolve Sonova's global intellectual property strategy, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives, innovation priorities, and market positioning.

• Serve as the principal advisor to the General Counsel, Executive Committee members, R&D leadership, and senior business leaders on intellectual property matters.

• Own enterprise-wide IP governance, risk management, and strategic decision-making across patents, trade secrets, trademarks, copyrights, and related intellectual property assets.

• Lead and develop senior IP professionals while fostering a business-oriented and strategically focused IP culture.

• Shape the future evolution of Sonova's IP function, capabilities, operating model, and external partnerships.

Strategic Partnership with R&D

• Serve as the primary strategic interface between the Legal and R&D organizations on all intellectual property matters.

• Ensure IP strategy is embedded throughout innovation processes, technology planning, product development, and long-term technology roadmaps.

• Maintain a permanent strategic presence within innovation planning and technology governance forums to identify and protect key innovations at the earliest stages of development.

• Guide strategic decisions concerning patents, trade secrets, design rights, publication strategies, open innovation initiatives, and alternative protection mechanisms.

• Partner closely with R&D leadership to ensure effective operation of invention harvesting processes, IP stage-gates, freedom-to-operate reviews, and technical risk assessments.

Portfolio Strategy & Investment Governance

• Establish the strategic direction for Sonova's global patent and design portfolio.

• Ensure portfolio investments are aligned with business priorities, technology trends, and competitive differentiation objectives.

• Oversee portfolio development, prosecution strategy, maintenance decisions, and lifecycle management through experienced internal teams and external counsel.

• Regularly assess portfolio strength, geographic coverage, white-space opportunities, competitive positioning, and emerging risks.

• Drive a disciplined approach to maximizing portfolio value and return on investment.

Competitive Intelligence & Strategic Risk Assessment

• Direct Sonova's IP-based competitive intelligence strategy, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities and technology objectives.

• Oversee strategic freedom-to-operate, clearance, and risk management frameworks across the organization.

• Translate complex competitive IP landscapes into actionable strategic recommendations for executive leadership.

• Monitor significant industry, regulatory, technological, and competitive developments impacting Sonova's innovation strategy.

• Identify opportunities for portfolio strengthening, strategic acquisitions, partnerships, licensing opportunities, and risk mitigation.

Licensing, Partnerships & Value Creation

• Lead the company's strategy for licensing, cross-licensing, technology partnerships, and other IP-based value creation initiatives.

• Support strategic commercial negotiations where intellectual property is a key business asset.

• Provide strategic IP leadership in M&A transactions, partnerships, collaborations, and technology investments.

• Evaluate opportunities to leverage Sonova's intellectual property portfolio as a competitive and commercial advantage.

Disputes, Enforcement & Litigation Strategy

• Define and direct Sonova's global strategy for IP enforcement, defense, and dispute resolution.

• Oversee significant patent, trademark, copyright, advertising, and technology-related disputes worldwide.

• Manage external counsel and expert advisors supporting contentious IP matters.

• Advise executive leadership on risk exposure, litigation strategy, settlement considerations, and business impacts.

• Ensure alignment between litigation strategy, portfolio development, and broader business objectives.

Soft IP Governance & Brand Protection

• Oversee enterprise management of trademarks, copyrights, brand protection, marketing claims, and related intellectual property matters.

• Ensure effective collaboration between Legal, Marketing, and Commercial functions to protect and enhance Sonova's brand assets.

• Establish frameworks that enable early review, clearance, and protection of brand and product naming initiatives.

• Support the development and protection of valuable intangible assets across the business.

Governance & Enterprise Risk Management

• Establish and maintain robust IP governance frameworks, policies, processes, and decision-making standards.

• Chair or actively participate in cross-functional governance forums responsible for intellectual property strategy, prioritization, and resource alignment.

• Ensure consistent and proactive management of IP-related risks across jurisdictions and business functions.

• Promote enterprise-wide awareness of intellectual property as a strategic business asset.

• Ensure effective utilization of external counsel, service providers, and supporting resources.

More about you:

• Advanced degree (JD, PhD, LLM, MSc Engineering, or equivalent) in a legal, scientific, engineering, or technical discipline.

• 15+ years of progressive intellectual property experience with significant exposure to patent strategy and counseling.

• Demonstrated success operating at a senior strategic level and influencing executive leadership and R&D organizations.

• Deep understanding of global patent systems and broader intellectual property frameworks.

• Experience leading IP organizations through senior professionals and external partners.

• Strong commercial orientation with the ability to balance legal, technical, business, and innovation considerations.

• Proven experience managing complex cross-functional stakeholder environments.

Preferred previous experience

• Experience within a multinational technology, healthcare, medical device, electronics, software, or innovation-driven organization.

• Significant experience in patent litigation, enforcement, oppositions, or dispute management in the US and Europe.

• Demonstrated success supporting strategic licensing, cross-licensing, technology transactions, collaborations, or M&A activities.

• Familiarity with U.S., European, and Asian intellectual property systems and regulatory environments.

• Experience partnering closely with engineering and R&D organizations in highly innovative environments.

Why Join Sonova

This is a rare opportunity to shape the intellectual property strategy of a global innovation leader operating at the intersection of healthcare and technology.

You will have direct influence on innovation strategy, technology direction, competitive positioning, and enterprise value creation while partnering closely with world-class R&D, legal, and business leaders. The role offers exceptional visibility, meaningful impact, and the opportunity to help define the future of intellectual property at Sonova.

jobs.description:
Location: Stäfa, Switzerland

Fulltime, 6–9 Months

Our team develops and optimizes manufacturing processes, defines production parameters, supports ongoing products in production, and collaborates closely with manufacturing sites around the world. To strengthen our team, we are looking for a motivated Practical Trainee who is eager to apply scientific knowledge to real-world engineering challenges.

In this role, you will support our team in investigating and understanding complex material systems used in hearing aid manufacturing. A particular focus will be on the protection of solder joints against corrosion through specialized coating technologies.

Your Responsibilities

• Characterize and evaluate material systems, solder joints, and protective coating technologies

• Support the development of internal testing standards for corrosion protection technologies

• Conduct laboratory experiments, technology analyses, and feasibility studies

• Organize and perform various measurements in our test and analysis laboratory

• Analyze and interpret experimental data and measurement results

• Prepare technical reports and documentation

Your Profile

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master's degree in Materials Science, Physical Chemistry or a related scientific or engineering discipline

• Strong interest in materials, manufacturing technologies, and laboratory work

• Analytical and structured way of thinking

• Independent and proactive working style

• Good written and verbal communication skills in English (German is a plus)

• First exposure to laboratory testing and technical documentation

• Knowledge of material characterization methods is a plus

What We Offer

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model.

We can offer you a new challenge, with interesting tasks and much more – including an open corporate culture, flat hierarchies, support for further training and development, opportunities to take on responsibility, and an excellent range of foods, sports and cultural facilities.

• A hands-on role with real impact on manufacturing processes and product reliability

• Access to modern laboratories and testing equipment #LI-NB1

descriptionByLocale.it:
Ubicazione: Stäfa, Svizzera

A tempo pieno, 6–9 Mesi

Il nostro team sviluppa e ottimizza i processi produttivi, definisce i parametri di produzione, supporta i prodotti in corso nella produzione e collabora strettamente con i siti produttivi di tutto il mondo. Per rafforzare il nostro team, stiamo cercando un addestratore pratico motivato che è desideroso di applicare la conoscenza scientifica alle sfide di ingegneria del mondo reale.

In questo ruolo, supporterete il nostro team nell'indagine e nella comprensione di sistemi materiali complessi utilizzati nella produzione di apparecchi acustici. Un particolare focus sarà sulla protezione delle giunzioni di saldatura contro la corrosione attraverso tecnologie di rivestimento specializzate.

Le tue responsabilità

• Caratterizzare e valutare i sistemi materiali, le giunzioni di saldatura e le tecnologie di rivestimento protettivo

• Sostenere lo sviluppo di standard di test interni per le tecnologie di protezione della corrosione

• Condurre esperimenti di laboratorio, analisi tecnologiche e studi di fattibilità

• Organizzare e eseguire varie misurazioni nel nostro laboratorio di test e analisi

• Analizzare e interpretare i dati sperimentali e i risultati delle misurazioni

• Preparare relazioni tecniche e documentazione

Il tuo profilo

• Attualmente perseguire o recentemente completato un Master in Scienze dei Materiali, Chimica Fisica o una disciplina scientifica o ingegneristica correlata

• Forte interesse per materiali, tecnologie di produzione e lavori di laboratorio

• Analitico e strutturato modo di pensare

• Stile di lavoro indipendente e proattivo

• Buone capacità di comunicazione scritte e verbali in inglese (il tedesco è un plus)

• Prima esposizione a test di laboratorio e documentazione tecnica

• La conoscenza dei metodi di caratterizzazione materiale è un plus

Cosa offriamo

Come uno dei principali fornitori di servizi per l’udito con sede in Svizzera, ci impegniamo a costruire una cultura inclusiva. Vogliamo creare un ambiente in cui è possibile bilanciare una carriera di successo con i vostri impegni e interessi al di fuori del lavoro, attraverso il nostro modello di lavoro ibrido flessibile.

Possiamo offrirvi una nuova sfida, con compiti interessanti e molto altro – tra cui una cultura aziendale aperta, gerarchie piatte, supporto per ulteriori formazione e sviluppo, opportunità di assumersi la responsabilità, e un'eccellente gamma di alimenti, strutture sportive e culturali.

• Un ruolo pratico con un impatto reale sui processi produttivi e sull'affidabilità dei prodotti

• Accesso ai moderni laboratori e attrezzature di prova #LI-NB1

jobs.description:
As Senior Manager Hearing Performance, you will shape how Sonova’s next generation of hearing instruments perform and sound in the real world. You will lead a team of hearing performance engineers and Functional Experts and take end-to-end ownership of translating cutting-edge algorithmic innovation into measurable end-user benefit and outstanding sound experiences.

Working at the intersection of audiology, signal processing, deep learning and system integration, you will turn strategy into execution, guide innovation from early concepts through to productization, and bring together experts across R&D and Marketing. In return for your engineering expertise, strategic thinking and leadership, you will have the opportunity to influence the future of hearing performance at scale and make a meaningful difference to millions of people worldwide.

More about the role

• Own and drive the end-to-end hearing performance of Sonova’s algorithmic innovations, ensuring industry-leading end-user benefit and outstanding sound experience.

• Lead, develop and empower a team of hearing performance engineers, creating clear priorities, strong ownership and a culture of technical excellence.

• Shape new hearing functions, algorithms and features from early ideation and prototyping through development, verification and productization.

• Drive evidence-based decisions by leading technical measurements, performance evaluations and testing, while identifying key performance gaps and opportunities for differentiation.

• Partner closely with Signal Processing, Deep Learning, Audiological Innovation, Controller Software, Marketing and other R&D domains to translate innovation into high-performing products.

• Translate strategy and functional roadmaps into clear, achievable team objectives, balancing innovation, end-user benefit, quality, scalability, resources and timelines.

• Continuously advance development practices, tools and infrastructure, including the use of AI technologies, while ensuring compliance with R&D processes, quality standards and regulatory expectations.

More about you

• Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in Electrical Engineerig, Physics, , Acoustics, Biomedical Engineering, or a closely related scientific or technical discipline.

• At least 5 years of relevant experience in sound processing, engineering, or MedTech R&D, combined with significant senior technical or functional leadership experience.

• Proven track record of leading people, complex technical delivery and cross-functional collaboration in an international, multi-site environment.

• Ability to connect scientific and technical expertise with user needs and business priorities.

• Strategic and analytical mindset with the confidence to make decisions, manage trade-offs and create clarity in complex or uncertain environments.

• Collaborative and empowering leadership style, with strong communication skills and a passion for developing people, building capabilities and driving technological change.

• Fluent English; German and experience with medical device regulations, validation frameworks or data-driven development environments are an advantage.

More about what we offer

As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both your professional and personal development, and there are exceptional growth opportunities with individual development plans.
